papers.title: AI-driven discovery and validation of a GIPC1 PDZ domain inhibitor for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains highly aggressive, with a five-year survival rate under 13.3%, due to late diagnosis, rapid progression, and therapeutic resistance, highlighting the need for advanced treatments. GAIP-interacting protein C terminus 1 (GIPC1), a scaffolding protein overexpressed in PDAC, drives tumor growth and chemoresistance but has remained "undruggable" due to its PDZ domain. Using advanced computational modeling, machine learning, and predictive analytics, we identified a selective and specific small molecule inhibitor of GIPC1 (GIPCi) targeting its PDZ doma
papers.summary: This study uses AI-driven computational modeling and machine learning to identify a small molecule inhibitor (GIPCi) targeting the PDZ domain of GIPC1, a scaffolding protein overexpressed in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). The inhibitor shows selectivity and potential to block GIPC1's tumor-promoting and chemoresistance functions, offering a new therapeutic avenue for this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: Retraction Note: A diagnostic model for sepsis using an integrated machine learning framework approach and its therapeutic drug discovery.
papers.summary: This is a retraction note for a previously published article on a sepsis diagnostic model. The article has been retracted, meaning its findings should not be relied upon.

papers.title: The Potential of AI-Driven High-Content Imaging in Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: We have authored a compelling and timely review that highlights the transformative potential of high-content imaging for discovering small molecules (SMs). SMs are crucial for advancing drug potency, selectivity, and precision, and their assessment through specialized cellular assays accelerates drug development. High-content imaging (HCI), which seamlessly integrates automated microscopy with sophisticated image analysis powered by artificial intelligence (AI), is revolutionizing cell-based assays by enabling a comprehensive evaluation of cellular parameters following drug treatment. The rich
papers.summary: This review highlights the transformative potential of combining high-content imaging with AI for drug discovery, enabling comprehensive evaluation of cellular responses to small molecules. It emphasizes how this approach accelerates drug development by improving potency, selectivity, and precision assessment.

papers.title: Agentic and Generative AI for Drug Discovery.
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging roles of agentic and generative AI in drug discovery, covering applications in target identification, molecular design, and clinical trial optimization. It highlights how these technologies can accelerate the drug development pipeline while also addressing challenges such as data quality, model interpretability, and regulatory considerations.

papers.title: Deep learning-based prediction of drug-target interactions between antiviral drugs and SARS-CoV-2 proteins using an image-based representation approach.
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing offers a time-efficient strategy for identifying therapeutics against emerging pathogens such as SARS-CoV-2. In this study, we apply MPS2IT-DTI (Molecule and Protein Sequence to Image Transformer for Drug-Target Interaction), a deep learning framework that represents molecular (SMILES) and protein (FASTA) sequences as images using k-mer frequency encoding, enabling convolutional neural networks to capture spatial compositional patterns associated with biochemical interactions. A curated dataset (BindingDB-FDA) containing 83,165 binding interactions from 1640 FDA-approved ligan
papers.summary: This study applies a deep learning framework (MPS2IT-DTI) that converts drug and protein sequences into images via k-mer frequency encoding to predict drug-target interactions, specifically for antiviral drugs against SARS-CoV-2 proteins. The approach leverages convolutional neural networks on a curated FDA-approved drug dataset, demonstrating a novel image-based representation for drug repurposing.

papers.title: [Advances in the application of artificial intelligence in antimicrobial resistance research].
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has emerged as a major threat to global public health, while conventional research methods face severe bottlenecks in deciphering its complex mechanisms and accelerating new drug development. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, is revolutionizing AMR research by enabling the processing of high-dimensional multi-omics data, uncovering hidden patterns, and generating novel hypotheses. This review systematically elaborates on the biomedical big data ecosystem that drives the AI revolution, including multi-omics data, phenotypic and clinical dat
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence, especially deep learning, is transforming antimicrobial resistance (AMR) research by enabling analysis of high-dimensional multi-omics and clinical data to uncover hidden patterns and accelerate drug development. It systematically outlines the biomedical big data ecosystem that supports AI-driven approaches in AMR.

papers.title: [Artificial intelligence-based mining of antimicrobial peptides in the microbiome].
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are small-molecule polypeptides with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity that are induced by the innate immune system of organisms and constitute a crucial component of the innate immune defense. With the misuse of antibiotics and other antimicrobial agents, the problem of bacterial resistance has become increasingly severe. Naturally occurring AMPs derived from the microbiome, owing to their broad availability, stable physicochemical properties, relatively low propensity to induce resistance, and capacity to contribute to the maintenance of commensal microbiota
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to mine antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) from microbiome data, highlighting their potential as alternatives to conventional antibiotics in the face of rising antimicrobial resistance. It covers AI-based approaches for discovering naturally occurring AMPs, which are valued for their broad availability, stability, and low resistance propensity.

papers.title: Quantum convolutional HLA immunogenic peptide prediction (Q-CHIPP): Next-generation neoantigen prediction with quantum neural network.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of quantum computing is driven by promises of performing complex calculations with unprecedented speed; however, current use cases have been limited by quantum hardware and the difficulty of identifying problems that classical computers cannot easily address. Within these constraints, biological problems including drug discovery, protein folding, and precision medicine present an opportunity to understand how current quantum hardware can make advances. In immunology, accurate prediction of cancer neoantigens remains a major challenge, limited by small, noisy datasets and the i
papers.summary: This paper introduces Q-CHIPP, a quantum convolutional neural network for predicting HLA immunogenic peptides (neoantigens), addressing the challenge of small, noisy datasets in immunology. The authors demonstrate that their quantum approach achieves competitive or improved performance compared to classical methods, highlighting a practical use case for current quantum hardware in precision medicine.

papers.title: EcoXAI: Autonomous Agentic Ecosystem for Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Biomedical Discovery.
papers.abstract: As biomedical datasets and knowledge graphs continue to grow in size, complexity, and heterogeneity, navigating and extracting actionable insights from them presents a major bottleneck for researchers. There is a clear need for autonomous analytical solutions that can utilize recent advancements in agentic AI such as agent harnessing and loop engineering without introducing hallucination or workflow fragmentation. Researchers, regardless of technical expertise, need tools that streamline complex data analysis and deliver meaningful, actionable insights grounded in both data and established bio
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: EcoXAI is an autonomous agentic AI ecosystem designed to streamline biomedical data analysis by integrating explainable AI and knowledge graphs, aiming to reduce hallucinations and workflow fragmentation. It provides researchers with tools to extract actionable insights from complex, heterogeneous biomedical datasets without requiring deep technical expertise.

papers.title: GEM-GPT Enables Personalized Cell Type-Resolved Therapeutic Design for Systems Pharmacology.
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful framework for drug discovery, yet most current approaches follow one-drug-one-gene target-based paradigms that struggle to capture the complexity and heterogeneity of chronic and systemic diseases. Omics-driven systems pharmacology provides a promising strategy to overcome these limitations, but generative AI tools specifically designed for systems pharmacology-oriented drug design remain scarce. To address this gap, we introduce GEM-GPT, a transcriptomics-based molecule generation framework that designs personalized therapeutic
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: GEM-GPT is a new generative AI framework that designs personalized therapeutic molecules based on transcriptomics data, moving beyond single-target drug discovery to capture the complexity of systemic diseases. It enables cell type-resolved drug design, offering a systems pharmacology approach tailored to individual patients.

papers.title: Mol2Image: an enhanced DDI prediction framework leveraging drug molecular descriptors.
papers.abstract: Drug-drug interactions (DDIs) are a critical safety issue in clinical practice, as they can lead to severe and often unpredictable adverse effects. This risk becomes significantly higher in multi-drug therapies, which are increasingly used in the treatment of complex and chronic diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular disorders, and diabetes. However, identifying DDIs through in vivo studies is costly and time-consuming. In this study, a novel DDI prediction model, Mol2Image, has been proposed that utilizes chemical structure features derived from Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (
papers.summary: Mol2Image is a new computational model that predicts drug-drug interactions by converting drug molecular structures into image-like representations, enabling more accurate and efficient DDI risk assessment without costly lab experiments. The approach leverages chemical structure features from SMILES notation and demonstrates improved predictive performance, offering a practical tool for safer multi-drug therapy planning.

papers.title: Methods for the establishment of enzymatic mechanisms - from QM to ML.
papers.abstract: We offer a practical and conceptual introduction to some of the current approaches to modelling enzymatic reaction mechanisms, ranging from quantum mechanics (QM), molecular mechanics (MM), and hybrid QM/MM approaches to enhanced sampling methods, knowledge-based approaches, and machine learning (ML) advances. We discuss how static and dynamic QM/MM approaches, as well as multi-PES strategies, have contributed to understanding the role of conformational diversity, electrostatic preorganization and solvent participation in the determination of catalytic barriers and reaction paths. We focus on
papers.summary: This review provides a practical introduction to computational methods for modeling enzymatic reaction mechanisms, covering quantum mechanics, molecular mechanics, hybrid QM/MM approaches, enhanced sampling, and machine learning. It highlights how these techniques reveal the roles of conformational dynamics, electrostatic preorganization, and solvent in catalysis.

papers.title: Integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic perturbation resources reveals complementary therapeutic spaces for drug repurposing.
papers.abstract: Transcriptome-based drug repurposing can accelerate therapeutic discovery, but is limited by fragmented resources, inconsistent quality control, and reliance on single perturbation databases. We developed CDRPipe (Computational Drug Repurposing Pipeline), a unified framework that interrogates disease signatures against drug perturbation signatures generated by distinct experimental technologies. Specifically, CDRPipe harmonizes microarray perturbation profiles from the Connectivity Map (CMap; 1,968 quality-filtered experiments) with pseudo-bulk profiles derived from large-scale single-cell RNA
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed CDRPipe, a computational pipeline that integrates drug perturbation data from both bulk microarray (CMap) and single-cell RNA-seq sources to enable more comprehensive drug repurposing. By harmonizing these complementary datasets, CDRPipe expands the therapeutic search space and improves the identification of potential drug-disease connections.

papers.title: Characterization of Forestiera tomentosa Fruit: Proximate Composition, Physicochemical Parameters, Phenolic Content, Antioxidant Capacity, and Toxicological Assessment.
papers.abstract: The demand for sustainable nutrients and bioactive compounds has increased interest in underutilized wild plants. Forestiera tomentosa, a Mexican drupe-bearing species, is largely unexplored. This study evaluated the proximate composition, physicochemical and functional properties, phenolic profile, antioxidant capacity, and toxicological safety of F. tomentosa fruit. The fruit showed high carbohydrate content [71.94% dry weight (DW)], with notable crude fiber (7.90% DW), protein (7.39% DW), and lipid (4.30% DW) contents. Analysis revealed a mildly acidic pH (5.66), titratable acidity of 0.32%
papers.summary: This study characterizes the nutritional and functional properties of the underutilized Mexican fruit Forestiera tomentosa, revealing high carbohydrate and fiber content, moderate protein and lipid levels, and a mildly acidic pH. The fruit also contains phenolic compounds with antioxidant capacity, and toxicological assessment indicates safety, supporting its potential as a sustainable food source.

papers.title: Drug Repurposing as a Broad-Spectrum Strategy Against Coronaviruses: Frontiers in Mechanisms and Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Coronaviruses (family Coronaviridae) are enveloped, positive-sense, single-stranded RNA viruses with broad host adaptability. They transmit across species among humans, livestock, companion animals, and wildlife, eliciting a disease spectrum ranging from mild respiratory and gastrointestinal symptoms to fatal multi-organ failure, thereby posing significant challenges to global health. In this context, drug repurposing has emerged as a practical strategy for rapidly identifying broad-spectrum antivirals against emerging and re-emerging coronaviruses. Using coronaviruses as a paradigm, this revi
papers.summary: This review discusses drug repurposing as a strategy to identify broad-spectrum antivirals against coronaviruses, covering mechanisms of action and clinical translation. It highlights the challenges posed by coronaviruses and the potential of repurposing existing drugs to accelerate pandemic response.

papers.title: An Integrative Bioinformatics Framework Prioritises a Gingival Mesenchymal Stem Cell Paracrine Apoptosis-ROS Axis in HPV-Negative Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Preliminary Experimental Support and Repurposable-Drug Hypotheses.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) accounts for most head-and-neck cancers, and effective biological adjuvants remain limited. Gingival mesenchymal stem cells (GMSCs) exhibit anti-tumour paracrine activity, but the underlying molecular mechanisms and their relevance in patient cohorts remain incompletely understood. Consensus apoptosis-reactive oxygen species (ROS) effectors were identified through integrated transcriptomic analyses of TCGA-HNSC and three GEO cohorts. Candidate genes were evaluated in primary OSCC cells exposed to GMSC-conditioned medium or indirect Transwell co-culture. Find
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative bioinformatics approach to identify a paracrine apoptosis-ROS axis in gingival mesenchymal stem cells (GMSCs) that may suppress HPV-negative oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). The authors prioritized candidate genes through transcriptomic analyses of TCGA and GEO cohorts and provided preliminary experimental support using OSCC cells exposed to GMSC-conditioned medium, along with hypotheses for repurposable drugs.

papers.title: Repurposing FDA-Approved Drugs as Nav1.7 Channel Modulators: An Integrated Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: The voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.7 is a strongly validated target for the development of novel, non-opioid analgesics due to its genetic link to pain signaling. To accelerate the discovery of safe Nav1.7 modulators, this study outlines an integrated computational pipeline to repurpose FDA-approved drugs. A structurally complete model of the Nav1.7 central pore was generated via homology modeling from a high-resolution cryo-EM structure (PDB: 7W9K) to ensure a physically consistent model suitable for dynamic simulations. We conducted a structure-based virtual screening of 2296 FDA-approved
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to repurpose FDA-approved drugs as modulators of the Nav1.7 sodium channel, a validated target for non-opioid pain relief. By building a complete structural model and screening 2296 approved drugs, the authors identify potential candidates that could be fast-tracked for pain therapy.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Hyperspectral Interferometry and Single-Cell Dispersion Imaging.
papers.abstract: Interferometry techniques are essential for extracting phase information from optical systems enabling precise measurements of dispersion and highly sensitive detection of perturbations. While phase sensing offers enhanced sensitivity compared to conventional spectroscopy methods, this sensitivity often makes systems more vulnerable to external factors such as vibrations, introducing instability and noise. In this work, we demonstrate a broadband and AI-enhanced interferometry method, denoted general polarization common-path interferometry (GPCPI) that relaxes the polarization constraints of t
papers.summary: This paper presents a new AI-enhanced interferometry technique (GPCPI) that improves stability and sensitivity for measuring optical dispersion, and applies it to single-cell imaging. The method relaxes polarization constraints and uses AI to mitigate noise from vibrations, enabling more precise single-cell dispersion measurements.

papers.title: CovSite: A High-Throughput Blind Covalent Screening Framework for Reactive Site Detection.
papers.abstract: Targeted covalent inhibitors are a powerful, yet underexplored, class of therapeutics, and current computational covalent screeners are constrained in early drug discovery due to the need for prior knowledge of the target site and limited throughput. We present CovSite, a blind covalent screening tool that identifies candidate reactive residues across the entire protein surface, utilizing only the protein structure and electrophile SMILES. CovSite applies a pipeline of four orthogonal physicochemical filters (nucleophile identification, solvent accessibility, environment-dependent deprotonatio
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CovSite is a new computational tool for blind covalent drug screening that identifies reactive residues across the entire protein surface without prior knowledge of the target site. It uses only the protein structure and electrophile SMILES, applying four orthogonal physicochemical filters to rank candidate sites, which could accelerate early drug discovery for covalent inhibitors.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Virtual Screening Identifies Potential Small-Molecule Inhibitors of ASK1: Natural Product Lead Discovery for MASH.
papers.abstract: Apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1 (ASK1) represents a critical therapeutic target for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Natural products, owing to their unique chemical diversity, constitute a rich reservoir for discovering novel ASK1 inhibitors. The emergence of artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery (AIDD) has opened new avenues for exploring small-molecule inhibitors. Through virtual screening, molecular docking, interaction profiling, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM-GBSA binding free energy calculations, we systematically evaluated the binding mode
papers.summary: This study uses deep learning-based virtual screening combined with molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and binding free energy calculations to identify natural product small-molecule inhibitors of ASK1, a key therapeutic target for MASH. The approach successfully pinpoints promising lead compounds with favorable binding modes, offering a new avenue for natural product-based drug discovery against this liver disease.

papers.title: Experimental and Computational Insights into the Apoptotic Potential of New Phenanthroline-Based Copper(II) Complexes: From Spectroscopic Characterization and In Vitro Cytotoxicity to In Silico Target Identification.
papers.abstract: Background: Two novel copper(II) coordination complexes, PH-Cu [(1,10-phenanthroline)(malonato)copper(II)] and PC-Cu [(1,10-phenanthroline)(cyclobutane-1,1-dicarboxylato)copper(II)], were synthesized and evaluated as potential anticancer agents, aiming to characterize structural properties, explore antiproliferative activity and generate mechanistic hypotheses through experimental and computational approaches. Methods: Complexes were characterized by EPR, FTIR-ATR, and ESI-MS, with preliminary SC-XRD data for PH-Cu. Antiproliferative activity was evaluated against six human cancer cell lines u
papers.summary: This study synthesizes and characterizes two novel copper(II) complexes with phenanthroline ligands, evaluating their anticancer potential across six human cancer cell lines. Using spectroscopic methods and computational target identification, the authors propose apoptotic mechanisms, offering a foundation for developing these complexes as anticancer drug candidates.

papers.title: AUKAT: Conditional VAE-Driven Augmentation and Neural Modeling of Enzyme Turnover Numbers.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of enzyme turnover numbers (kcat) is essential for applications in systems biology, metabolic engineering, and drug discovery, yet remains challenging due to the limited availability and uneven distribution of experimental data. Here, we present AUKAT, an integrated framework that combines conditional generative modeling with deep neural prediction to improve kcat estimation. A conditional variational autoencoder generates synthetic training instances in embedding space, followed by a selection pipeline that retains samples with strong agreement across independent evaluator
papers.summary: AUKAT is a new computational framework that uses a conditional variational autoencoder to generate synthetic training data for predicting enzyme turnover numbers (kcat), addressing the problem of limited and unevenly distributed experimental data. The approach improves kcat estimation accuracy by augmenting training datasets with high-quality synthetic samples, which could benefit systems biology, metabolic engineering, and drug discovery applications.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology Guided Drug Repurposing and Molecular Modeling Identify Sulfasalazine as a Potential OXA-23 β-Lactamase in Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii has become a major health concern, primarily driven by the dissemination of class D β-lactamases, particularly OXA-23, which compromise the efficacy of last-line β-lactam antibiotics. Drug repurposing combined with structure-based computational approaches provides a promising strategy for accelerating the discovery of novel therapeutic candidates against multidrug-resistant pathogens. This study aimed to identify FDA-approved non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS) with potential inhibitory activity against OXA-23 β-lac
papers.summary: This study used network pharmacology and molecular modeling to screen FDA-approved NSAIDs for potential inhibitors of the OXA-23 β-lactamase, which drives carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii. Sulfasalazine was identified as a promising candidate, suggesting a potential drug repurposing strategy to combat multidrug-resistant infections.

papers.title: Ligand Design Using Unique Conformations to Preferentially Dock a Specific Site on Collagen-Bound MMP1.
papers.abstract: Precise site-specific ligand design remains a major challenge in structure-based drug discovery. Most existing approaches screen ligands against binding pockets identified from static protein structures obtained by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, cryo-electron microscopy, or AlphaFold predictions. However, protein function is governed by a structure-dynamics-function relationship, and ligand screening that does not account for binding competition across the protein surface or the receptor's dynamic, substrate-dependent conformational states remains incomplete. Substrate-specific confo
papers.summary: This study presents a ligand design strategy that leverages unique protein conformations to achieve site-specific docking on collagen-bound MMP1, addressing the limitations of static-structure-based drug discovery. By accounting for the receptor's dynamic, substrate-dependent states, the approach improves selectivity for a particular binding site.

papers.title: Using Deep Learning Models of Gene Regulation to Guide Drug Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Background: Drug repurposing offers a cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic discovery, but most computational approaches do not model noncoding genetic variation. Because over 90% of genome-wide association study (GWAS) risk variants reside in noncoding regions, linking regulatory variation to therapeutic hypotheses remains a major challenge. Methods: We developed an integrative deep learning framework that links allele-specific enhancer prediction to candidate therapeutics through two complementary prioritization strategies, a transcription factor (TF)-based and a gene-based appro
papers.summary: This paper presents an integrative deep learning framework that links noncoding genetic variants to drug repurposing candidates by combining allele-specific enhancer prediction with transcription factor and gene-based prioritization strategies. The approach addresses the challenge that most GWAS risk variants are noncoding, offering a new computational tool for therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: Integral Lipophilicity Studies with in Silico ADMET Parameter Analysis of Novel Pseudothiohydantoin Derivatives.
papers.abstract: This article describes the assessment of the lipophilicity of 18 new pseudothiohydantoin (2-aminothiazol-4(5H)-one) derivatives using experimental and computational methods. Previous studies have shown that the tested derivatives are inhibitors of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 and inhibit the metabolic activity of selected cancer cell lines. Lipophilicity, as log kw and RM0, was determined using reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) and reversed-phase thin-layer chromatography (RP-TLC), respectively. In both chromatographic methods, methanol served as a modi
papers.summary: This study evaluates the lipophilicity of 18 novel pseudothiohydantoin derivatives using experimental chromatographic methods and computational ADMET predictions. The findings provide key physicochemical parameters that support the drug-likeness and potential bioavailability of these compounds, which are known inhibitors of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 and cancer cell metabolic activity.

papers.title: Protocol for Membrane Permeability Prediction of Cyclic Peptides Using Descriptors Obtained from Extended Ensemble Molecular Dynamics Simulations and Chemical Structures.
papers.abstract: Improving the membrane permeability is crucial in cyclic peptide drug discovery. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are widely used to analyze membrane permeability but are computationally expensive. Machine learning offers a low-cost alternative, but its performance is limited by the size of available experimental data sets and the difficulty of incorporating peptide-specific three-dimensional (3D) structural information. Although the 3D conformations of cyclic peptides are closely associated with membrane permeability, they are highly sensitive to subtle changes in the chemical structure. T
papers.summary: This protocol describes a machine learning approach for predicting the membrane permeability of cyclic peptides, using descriptors derived from extended ensemble molecular dynamics simulations combined with chemical structure information. The method aims to address the limitations of small experimental datasets and the challenge of incorporating 3D conformational data, offering a more accurate and computationally efficient alternative to pure MD simulations for cyclic peptide drug discovery.

papers.title: Repurposing Masitinib Mesylate as a Novel FOXM1 Inhibitor for the Treatment of Aggressive Solid Tumors: Preclinical Validation in Human Breast and Oral Cancer Cells and Organotypic Tumor Slice Culture.
papers.abstract: The Forkhead box M1 (FOXM1) transcription factor, recognized as a prominent oncogene, facilitates cell cycle progression and mitotic fidelity in aggressive cancers. Overexpression of FOXM1 is correlated with uncontrolled cell proliferation, metastasis, and poor prognosis. Despite its pivotal role in promoting genomic instability, cancer stemness, and metastasis, FOXM1 remains a clinically undruggable target. In this study, we identified masitinib mesylate, a small-molecule inhibitor known for its multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibition, targeting c-Kit, PDGFRα, and PDGFRβ, as well as Lyn, whi
papers.summary: This study identifies masitinib mesylate as a novel inhibitor of the FOXM1 transcription factor, a key oncogene in aggressive cancers. Preclinical validation in human breast and oral cancer cells and organotypic tumor slice cultures demonstrates its potential as a repurposed therapeutic for solid tumors.

papers.title: A Length-Adaptive LLM-Enhanced Method for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction.
papers.abstract: Drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction is central to drug repurposing. Although existing methods integrate multi-dimensional features and have achieved certain progress, they rely heavily on molecular structure or graph structure information. This makes it difficult to capture complex biomedical semantic associations, leading to insufficient semantic information. To address this issue, this paper proposes BioLA-DTI, a large language model (LLM)-enhanced method for drug-target interaction prediction. The method leverages LLMs to provide semantic information for drugs and proteins. Furthermore
papers.summary: This paper introduces BioLA-DTI, a method that uses large language models to enhance drug-target interaction prediction by incorporating biomedical semantic information from drugs and proteins, addressing the limitations of structure-based approaches. The method improves prediction accuracy by capturing complex semantic associations.

papers.title: BoltzOmics: Predicting genetic variant effects on drug binding with Boltz-2.
papers.abstract: A mechanistic understanding of how genetic variants alter drug-receptor binding is central to precision medicine, drug response prediction, and drug development. Yet, experimental mutation-drug profiling remains slow and expensive, while existing computational approaches often trade accuracy for scalability. We developed BoltzOmics, an interactive, open-source platform that integrates Boltz-2, a deep learning model for biomolecular structure prediction, to rapidly assess mutation effects on drug binding. Starting from amino acid sequences, the workflow queries databases for genetic variants, g
papers.summary: BoltzOmics is an open-source platform that uses the Boltz-2 deep learning model to predict how genetic variants affect drug-receptor binding, starting from amino acid sequences and querying variant databases. It aims to provide a fast and scalable alternative to experimental mutation-drug profiling, supporting precision medicine and drug development.

papers.title: Discovery of Anti-Neuroinflammatory Compounds in Alzheimer's Disease: Current Trends and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation in response to abnormal protein aggregates has been implicated as a critical mechanism in several neurodegenerative diseases, and the modulation of signaling pathways associated with inflammation is being explored as a potential strategy for new therapeutics. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), the neuroinflammation hypothesis also starts to influence the landscape of drug discovery in place of the previously regarded amyloid hypothesis. As such, the objective of this review is to compile recent advanced in the discovery of anti-neuroinflammatory compounds developed through
papers.summary: This review discusses the shift in Alzheimer's disease drug discovery from the amyloid hypothesis toward targeting neuroinflammation, highlighting recent advances in anti-neuroinflammatory compounds. It compiles current trends and future perspectives on modulating inflammatory signaling pathways as a therapeutic strategy for AD.

papers.title: MOZAIC: Compound Growth via In Silico Reactions and Global Optimization using Conformational Space Annealing.
papers.abstract: Fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) efficiently explores chemical space by combining small molecular fragments. Advances in computational methods are accelerating the development of algorithm- and AI-based approaches in FBDD. However, it should be noted that certain methods do not provide synthetic pathways to obtain the proposed compounds. Consequently, these molecules might not be synthesized easily.
papers.summary: MOZAIC is a computational tool for fragment-based drug discovery that grows molecular fragments into larger compounds using in silico reactions and global optimization via conformational space annealing. Unlike some AI-based methods, it provides synthetic pathways for the proposed compounds, making them more readily synthesizable.

papers.title: Integrated design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and computational mechanistic insights of novel benzanilide derivatives as VEGFR-2 targeted anticancer agents.
papers.abstract: VEGFR-2 is a key regulator of tumor angiogenesis and a validated target in anticancer drug discovery. In this study, a series of novel benzanilide derivatives (7a-7f and 9a-9b) were designed, synthesized, and evaluated as potential VEGFR-2 inhibitors. The design strategy was guided by key pharmacophoric requirements for VEGFR-2 inhibition. All compounds were synthesized successfully and characterized, then screened for in vitro cytotoxic activity against MCF-7, MDA-MB-231, HePG-2, and HCT-116 cancer cell lines, with WI-38 and WISH normal cells used for selectivity assessment. Among the tested
papers.summary: This study reports the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel benzanilide derivatives as potential VEGFR-2 inhibitors for anticancer therapy. The compounds showed cytotoxic activity against several cancer cell lines with selectivity over normal cells, and computational insights supported their mechanism of action.

papers.title: Coumarin-based dual kinase inhibitors targeting CDK6 and VEGFR-2: experimental and computational validation.
papers.abstract: A rational pharmacophore-guided strategy was employed to design and synthesize a series of novel coumarin derivatives as potential dual cyclin-dependent kinase 6 (CDK6) and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) inhibitors. Following structural characterization, the synthesized compounds were evaluated for their anticancer activity against MCF-7, MDA-MB-231, HepG-2, and HCT-116 cancer cell lines, together with normal WI-38 and WISH cells. Among the tested derivatives, compound 7e exhibited the highest potency, with IC50 values ranging from 3.80 to 6.35 µM, while demonstrating
papers.summary: This study describes the design and synthesis of novel coumarin derivatives as dual inhibitors of CDK6 and VEGFR-2, with compound 7e showing the most potent anticancer activity across multiple cancer cell lines. The work combines experimental evaluation with computational validation, supporting the potential of these compounds as leads for cancer therapy.

papers.title: Heterocyclic chemistry meets wound care: novel p-methyl-m-trifluoromethyl-phenyl-substituted pyrrol-2-one derivatives with antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity.
papers.abstract: Biofilm-associated infections represent a major challenge in the treatment of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens, particularly in chronic and wound-related infections where bacterial adherence and persistence reduce therapeutic efficacy. To address this issue, we report a rapid, economical, and efficient one-pot three-component synthesis of 19 novel bis(trifluoromethyl)-dimethyl-substituted dihydro-pyrrol-2-one derivatives, providing a promising scaffold for the development of new antimicrobial and anti-biofilm agents. The structures of the synthesized compounds were confirmed by NMR, FT-IR, MA
papers.summary: This paper describes the synthesis of 19 novel pyrrol-2-one derivatives with antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity, offering a promising scaffold for treating biofilm-associated wound infections. The compounds were produced via a rapid, economical one-pot three-component reaction and characterized by standard spectroscopic methods.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Antimicrobial Stewardship: From Clinical Decision Support to Public Health Action.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) continues to threaten the effectiveness of modern medicine and poses major public health challenges worldwide. Antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) programmes are essential to mitigate inappropriate antimicrobial use but are often resource-intensive and difficult to sustain. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have generated interest in its potential to support stewardship activities across clinical, operational, and public health domains.
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence can support antimicrobial stewardship programs across clinical, operational, and public health domains, addressing the challenge of antimicrobial resistance. It highlights AI's potential to optimize antimicrobial use and reduce resource burden, while likely discussing implementation considerations.

papers.title: DeorphaNN: Virtual screening of GPCR peptide agonists using AlphaFold-predicted active-state complexes and deep learning embeddings.
papers.abstract: Peptide-activated G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) regulate physiological processes through interaction with neuropeptides and peptide hormones. Identifying endogenous peptide agonists remains challenging, as peptide-GPCR pairings often follow gene-family relationships that offer limited predictive insight for orphan GPCRs without characterized homologs. Using a dataset of experimentally validated peptide-GPCR interactions from Caenorhabditis elegans, we demonstrate that AF-multimer confidence metrics partially discriminate agonist from non-agonist complexes, with improved discrimination us
papers.summary: DeorphaNN is a new computational method that combines AlphaFold-predicted active-state GPCR-peptide complexes with deep learning embeddings to virtually screen for peptide agonists, particularly for orphan GPCRs. The approach was validated using C. elegans peptide-GPCR interaction data, showing that AlphaFold confidence metrics can partially distinguish agonists from non-agonists, and the deep learning model improves this discrimination. This work offers a promising tool for deorphanizing GPCRs and identifying endogenous peptide ligands.

papers.title: Machine learning-based prediction of SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity: integrating IC50 regression and activity classification using multi-task neural networks.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of compound bioactivity is essential for accelerating antiviral drug discovery and reducing experimental costs. Machine learning (ML) methods have shown considerable promise in modeling structure-activity relationships and compound potency. In this study, we present an integrated ML framework for predicting IC50 and pIC50 values of compounds active against SARS-CoV-2, key indicators of antiviral potency. The proposed framework comprises three complementary approaches: (i) a regression model for quantitative IC50 prediction validated against experimental data; (ii) a classif
papers.summary: This study presents a machine learning framework that integrates regression and classification tasks to predict the bioactivity (IC50/pIC50) of compounds against SARS-CoV-2, aiming to accelerate antiviral drug discovery. The multi-task neural network approach demonstrates improved predictive accuracy for compound potency, offering a cost-effective computational tool for screening potential antiviral candidates.

papers.title: AI-driven Identification of Zika Virus Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Research engaged with AI has dramatically increased due to a huge improvement of technologies in terms of cost and time-effectiveness as well as decreasing use of animals. High throughput screening (HTS) is a frequently used method in drug discovery. Here, we combined two powerful tools for AI-driven identification of Zika virus (ZIKV) inhibitors. The main complication from ZIKV is microcephaly and other related birth defects when pregnant women become infected with this virus. To date, there are no specific vaccines and antiviral drugs for the treatment of ZIKV infection. We have successfully
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This study combines two AI-driven tools with high-throughput screening to identify potential inhibitors of the Zika virus, addressing the lack of specific vaccines and antiviral treatments. The approach demonstrates a cost- and time-effective strategy for drug discovery that reduces reliance on animal testing.

papers.title: AI-driven computational drug design: tools, workflow and challenges.
papers.abstract: Drug discovery is a time-consuming and resource-intensive process with a development period of more than ten years and a clinical attrition rate of more than 90%. Despite its contributions to rational drug design, computer-aided drug design has been constrained by limited scalability, overreliance on molecular descriptors, and incomplete modeling of complex biological systems. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed this landscape. AI-based drug discovery platforms have shifted the paradigm from a narrow focus to a comprehensive platform that covers target identification
papers.summary: This review discusses how AI is transforming computer-aided drug design by addressing limitations of traditional methods, such as scalability and reliance on molecular descriptors. It highlights AI-driven platforms that cover the entire drug discovery pipeline, from target identification to lead optimization, and outlines the workflow and remaining challenges.

papers.title: Discovery of Novel AURKA Inhibitors for Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) Therapy via a Hybrid Virtual Screening Pipeline, Biological Evaluation and Molecular Dynamics Simulation.
papers.abstract: Aurora kinase A (AURKA) is a pivotal driver of malignant progression and poor prognosis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). In this study, we developed a cascaded AI-driven virtual screening pipeline, integrating sequence-based affinity prediction (PSICHIC), equivariant deep learning docking (KarmaDock), and geometric rescoring (DeepDock) to identify novel AURKA inhibitor candidates. From an in-house 160,000-compound screening library assembled from commercially available collections, three leads (compounds 3, 5, and 8) were selected and subsequently validated via HTRF biochemical assays,
papers.summary: The authors developed a hybrid AI-driven virtual screening pipeline combining sequence-based affinity prediction, deep learning docking, and geometric rescoring to identify novel AURKA inhibitors for triple-negative breast cancer. Three lead compounds were validated in biochemical assays, demonstrating the pipeline's effectiveness in discovering potential therapeutic candidates.

papers.title: Inhibition of amyloid β aggregation by venetoclax: a computational and in vitro experimental approach.
papers.abstract: The aggregation of amyloid β-protein (Aβ) plays a key role in the pathological progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Given the current absence of effective therapeutic strategies, the drug repurposing approach provides novel insights into the treatment of AD. Venetoclax, a B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) inhibitor, has demonstrated remarkable efficacy in the treatment of hematological malignancies, characterized by well-defined pharmacokinetic properties and a favorable safety profile. However, its effects and molecular mechanisms in the treatment of AD remain unexplored. Here, we investigated th
papers.summary: This study explores venetoclax, an approved cancer drug, as a potential inhibitor of amyloid beta aggregation in Alzheimer's disease using computational and in vitro experiments. The findings suggest that venetoclax may interfere with Aβ aggregation, providing a basis for drug repurposing in AD treatment.

papers.title: Ziziphusine A, a unique plant-alkaloid featuring amide rotational isomerism from the fruits of Ziziphus jujuba with anti-inflammatory activity.
papers.abstract: Ziziphus jujuba var. inermis Rehder (Rhamnaceae) is an edible medicinal plant widely used in traditional medicine and functional foods. Phytochemical investigation of the methanolic extract of its fruits resulted in the isolation of a rare amide rotational isomeric alkaloid, ziziphusine A (1), together with eight known compounds including brassicasterol (2), (E)-24-nor-cholest-22-en-3β-ol (3), alphitolic acid (4), 3-O-cis-p-coumaroyl alphitolic acid (5), 3-O-trans-p-coumaroyl alphitolic acid (6), E-p-methoxycinnamic acid (7), (Z)-3-(4,5-dihydroxy-2-methoxyphenyl)acrylic acid (8), and scopoleti
papers.summary: Researchers isolated a new rare alkaloid, ziziphusine A, from jujube fruits, which exhibits amide rotational isomerism and shows anti-inflammatory activity, along with eight known compounds. This discovery adds a novel compound to the chemistry of Ziziphus jujuba and highlights its potential medicinal value.

papers.title: Identification and characterization of umami peptides from fermented soybean meal hydrolysates: Combined machine learning, cellular functional characterization, and structural interpretation.
papers.abstract: This study developed an efficient strategy for identifying umami and umami-enhancing peptides from fermented soybean meal hydrolysates (FSMH) to support the high-value utilization of soybean byproducts. An integrated approach combining virtual screening, molecular docking, sensory validation, intracellular calcium mobilization assays, and molecular dynamics simulation was employed. Sixteen peptides were synthesized for sensory validation, confirming 15 umami peptides. LE, AE, GEDLMVQ, and FEEINKV exhibited the strongest enhancement in both monosodium glutamate and inosinate/disodium guanylate
papers.summary: This study developed an integrated strategy combining machine learning, virtual screening, molecular docking, and cellular assays to identify umami and umami-enhancing peptides from fermented soybean meal hydrolysates. Fifteen of sixteen synthesized peptides were confirmed as umami peptides, with LE, AE, GEDLMVQ, and FEEINKV showing the strongest enhancement effects. The approach provides an efficient pipeline for discovering flavor peptides from food byproducts.

papers.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence Into Drug Discovery From Medicinal Plants: Current Applications and Infrastructural Challenges.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants represent a vast and evolutionarily refined reservoir of structurally diverse bioactive compounds that have historically contributed to major therapeutic breakthroughs. However, despite their pharmacological richness, systematic translation of plant-derived metabolites into clinically approved drugs remains constrained by persistent bottlenecks, including extract complexity, dereplication redundancy, structural elucidation challenges, taxonomic ambiguity, and multi-component pharmacology. This review presents a bottleneck-driven and systems-oriented framework for integrating a
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence can be integrated into drug discovery from medicinal plants, highlighting current applications and infrastructural challenges. It proposes a bottleneck-driven, systems-oriented framework to address issues like extract complexity, dereplication, and structural elucidation, aiming to improve the translation of plant-derived compounds into clinical drugs.

papers.title: Computational investigation for exploring botanical ingredients as potential negative allosteric modulators targeting metabotropic glutamate receptor 5.
papers.abstract: Metabotropic glutamate receptors are class C G-protein-coupled receptors that respond to the neurotransmitter glutamate. In particular, metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5) has been a valuable drug target for the management of psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders such as fragile X syndrome, autism, depression, anxiety, addiction, and movement disorders through negative allosteric modulators (NAMs). Despite the discovery of several NAMs, limited clinical efficacy was observed, thus preventing them from reaching the clinical stage. Natural products are indispensable, with a plethora
papers.summary: This computational study screened botanical ingredients as potential negative allosteric modulators (NAMs) of metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5), a drug target for psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. The findings identify promising natural compounds that may serve as leads for developing more effective mGluR5 NAMs with improved clinical efficacy.

papers.title: In silico discovery of CETP inhibitors from ZINC15 compounds using docking, ADMET filtering, and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Cholesteryl ester transfer protein is a crucial regulator of lipid metabolism and is considered a promising target for treating atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Given the clinical limitations and adverse effects of previous cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitors, such as torcetrapib, this study aimed to identify safer, more effective alternatives through computational drug discovery.
papers.summary: This study used computational methods to discover potential new inhibitors of cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) from the ZINC15 compound database, aiming to find safer alternatives to previous drugs like torcetrapib. Through docking, ADMET filtering, and molecular dynamics simulations, they identified promising candidates that could serve as leads for treating atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

papers.title: Antibacterial Activity of α-Sulfamidophosphonate Derivatives and Their In Silico Assessment as Dihydropteroate Synthase Binders.
papers.abstract: In this study, we report the first antibacterial evaluation of a focused library of 12 previously synthesized α-sulfamidophosphonate derivatives (4a-4l) against a panel of nine Gram-positive and Gram-negative strains, including ESBL- and carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales. The overall hit rate was modest, as most compounds were inactive at the highest tested concentration (MIC ≥ 256 µg/mL), indicating a narrow and strain-selective profile. Nevertheless, selected derivatives showed noteworthy activity against individual isolates: 4 g inhibited Staphylococcus aureus ATCC29213 at 4 µg/mL, 4
papers.summary: This study evaluates the antibacterial activity of 12 α-sulfamidophosphonate derivatives against a panel of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including drug-resistant strains. Most compounds showed weak activity, but one derivative (4g) exhibited notable inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus at 4 µg/mL, and in silico docking suggests these compounds may bind to dihydropteroate synthase, a key enzyme in folate biosynthesis.

papers.title: A call for principle-based acceptance of synthetic patients: establishing the AI-driven foundation for regulatory submissions.
papers.abstract: The pharmaceutical industry stands at the precipice of an AI-driven data revolution, with synthetic patients emerging as a transformative tool to accelerate drug discovery and development while enhancing patient privacy. However, a critical regulatory gap persists: the absence of a standardized basis from leading regulatory bodies for accepting AI-generated patient populations as evidence in regulatory submissions. This manuscript addresses this void by proposing five foundational principles-Representativeness, Utility, Robustness, Privacy Preservation, and Transparency-anchored by the "Fit fo
papers.summary: This paper proposes five foundational principles—Representativeness, Utility, Robustness, Privacy Preservation, and Transparency—to guide regulatory acceptance of AI-generated synthetic patients in drug development. It addresses the current lack of standardized regulatory guidance, aiming to establish a framework for using synthetic data in regulatory submissions.

papers.title: In silico drug discovery pipelines targeting antibiotic resistance: from genomes to leads.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is currently one of the leading global health threats. The evolution of drug-resistant bacterial pathogens is rapid, and there is a growing number of bacterial pathogens that have developed resistance to multiple antibiotics, and the rate at which new antibiotics are being developed is lagging far behind these two issues. In addition, historical drug discovery processes rely on conducting traditional in vitro-based studies to determine new antibiotics to use in practice. However, this process is becoming increasingly constricted due to high costs of conducting tr
papers.summary: This review discusses computational (in silico) drug discovery pipelines as a faster, more cost-effective alternative to traditional in vitro methods for identifying new antibiotics against resistant bacteria. It highlights how genomic and bioinformatics approaches can accelerate the discovery of leads to combat antimicrobial resistance, a major global health threat.

papers.title: Clinical AI-assisted FXR prioritization and WADDAICA-guided design of a berberine-inspired analogue for MASH: integrated computational and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), lack effective targeted therapies despite increasing global prevalence. The farnesoid X receptor (FXR) is a key regulator of hepatic lipid metabolism, inflammation, and fibrosis, making it a promising therapeutic target. However, existing FXR modulators are associated with limited efficacy and adverse effects.
papers.summary: This study uses clinical AI-assisted prioritization of the FXR target and a computational design approach (WADDAICA) to develop a berberine-inspired analogue for MASH, with integrated experimental validation. The work addresses the lack of effective targeted therapies for MASLD/MASH by proposing a novel FXR modulator with potentially improved efficacy and safety.

papers.title: Functional restoration of conformational (R175H) and contact (R273H) mutant p53 by Bacillus-derived Hydroxymycotrienin A in non-small cell lung cancer: a computational approach.
papers.abstract: The TP53 mutations in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) remain a formidable clinical challenge. Current strategies, using the covalent binder APR-246, are limited by off-target toxicity and resistance.
papers.summary: This computational study identifies Hydroxymycotrienin A, a Bacillus-derived compound, as a potential therapeutic agent for restoring function to two common mutant forms of p53 (R175H and R273H) in non-small cell lung cancer. Using molecular docking and dynamics simulations, the compound shows promise as an alternative to the current drug APR-246, which has toxicity and resistance issues.

papers.title: Uncovering the molecular landscape of young-onset diffuse gastric cancer: A relieff-based feature selection analysis on RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Diffuse Gastric Cancer (DGC) is an aggressive subtype with a poor prognosis and a lack of specific biomarkers, representing a critical unmet need in oncology. This study aimed to elucidate the key molecular drivers of DGC by integrating RNA-seq data with a multi-faceted bioinformatics approach.
papers.summary: This study uses a ReliefF-based feature selection method on RNA-seq data to identify key molecular drivers of young-onset diffuse gastric cancer (DGC), a subtype with poor prognosis and few biomarkers. The analysis reveals potential gene signatures and pathways that may serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets, addressing an unmet need in oncology.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses identify TRIP6 as a prognostic and EMT-associated biomarker in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by profound molecular heterogeneity and complex tumor-microenvironment interactions, which contribute to invasion, metastasis, and variable clinical outcomes. More effective prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets are still needed.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to identify TRIP6 as a prognostic biomarker associated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in colorectal cancer. The findings suggest TRIP6 may serve as a potential therapeutic target and prognostic indicator, highlighting its role in tumor invasion and metastasis.

papers.title: Bazedoxifene and Beyond: Identifying This SERM's Targets and Deciphering Its Molecular Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Bazedoxifene (BZA), a third-generation selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) approved for osteoporosis treatment, is attracting attention for drug repurposing, especially in cancer research. While designed primarily for estrogen receptors, BZA exhibits in vitro off-target interactions that may explain novel therapeutic benefits or account for potential side effects. This review comprehensively examines both established and newly identified targets of BZA beyond estrogen receptors. To gather relevant data, we reviewed over 1500 articles selecting key studies proposing insights into BZA t
papers.journal: Advances in pharmacological and pharmaceutical sciences
papers.summary: This review consolidates current knowledge on bazedoxifene (BZA), a third-generation SERM, focusing on its off-target interactions beyond estrogen receptors that may underlie its repurposing potential in cancer and other diseases. By synthesizing findings from over 1500 articles, the authors catalog BZA's newly identified targets and discuss the molecular mechanisms that could explain both its therapeutic benefits and side effects.

papers.title: Network pharmacology and molecular modelling analysis of Arctium lappa phytochemicals in valproic acid-induced hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Valproic acid (VPA) is an antiepileptic drug commonly employed to treat epilepsy. Despite this, the clinical application of VPA is often hindered by adverse reactions. This study aims to investigate the therapeutic potential of phytochemicals obtained from Arctium lappa to mitigate VPA-induced toxicity and to determine the mechanisms involved.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular modeling to investigate whether phytochemicals from Arctium lappa (greater burdock) can counteract liver and pancreatic toxicity caused by the antiepileptic drug valproic acid. The findings identify key bioactive compounds and their potential protein targets, suggesting a mechanistic basis for their protective effects.

papers.title: Integrated in silico and experimental evaluation of enhanced antioxidant effects of Mentha species using mixture design methodology.
papers.abstract: The search for strongly effective and safe antioxidants is still one of the most important objectives targeted by the food and pharmaceutical industry. The growing concerns about the risks posed by synthetic additives have led to research into natural sources of antioxidants, especially essential oils (EOs). The combination of different essential oils may amplify the free radical scavenging activity by introducing more diversity into the mixture of chemicals. In this research, we investigated the antioxidant activity of three essential oils derived from Mentha longifolia, Mentha aquatica, and
papers.summary: This study uses a mixture design approach to evaluate and optimize the antioxidant activity of essential oils from three Mentha species, finding that specific combinations enhance free radical scavenging compared to individual oils. The work integrates in silico modeling with experimental validation to identify synergistic blends.

papers.title: Druggable Mendelian randomization prioritizes CDH2 and supports finerenone as a candidate therapeutic strategy for diabetic retinopathy.
papers.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy remains a major cause of vision loss, and therapeutic strategies beyond anti-vascular endothelial growth factor treatment are still needed. This study aimed to identify genetically supported druggable targets for diabetic retinopathy and to evaluate finerenone as a candidate therapeutic intervention in experimental retinopathy. We performed druggable Mendelian randomization by integrating druggable-gene resources, blood cis-expression quantitative trait locus data, and a large genome-wide association dataset for diabetic retinopathy. Significant genes were further evaluate
papers.summary: This study used druggable Mendelian randomization to identify genetically supported drug targets for diabetic retinopathy, prioritizing CDH2 as a promising candidate. It also provided experimental evidence supporting finerenone as a potential therapeutic strategy, offering new avenues beyond current anti-VEGF treatments.
